_note: Batch 5.3 (F20) seeded campus happenings. Single source: tools/gen_engine.py injects this into the engine. Each is small, NPC-free (the narrator picks who is involved) and grounded in lore. where = a location name from data/locations.json ('' = campus-wide). from/to = hours. days: weekday | weekend | any | list. months: [first, last] (optional). weeks: list (optional). weight: relative odds. v1.1.0: outdoor = true for items that happen out of doors (skipped when the day's morning or afternoon has heavy rain, a storm, a blizzard or hail; Weather effects Full only). weather = the item appears only in that weather (Full only): snow (snow last night or this morning), after_storm (a lightning storm or a gale yesterday), dense_fog (dense fog this morning), clear_night (tonight's sky is clear; applies whenever weather is on, because the text states the sky). after_storm_x3: weight x3 on the day after a storm or gale.

items.text: A paid-work opening is up on the Notice Board: Menagerie mucking out, 40 points a shift. It will be gone by tomorrow.
The Main Library has posted a shelving shift on the Notice Board, the quiet kind that is rarely advertised twice.
A second-year has pinned a tutoring offer to the Notice Board: combat footwork, paid in points or in favours.
A lost-item note on the Notice Board: a silver-banded focus wand, last seen near the Lecture Halls. Reward offered.
Two Doves are walking the Courtyards slowly, watching faces. Students keep finding reasons to be somewhere else.
Something small has slipped its pen at the Menagerie; handlers are combing the Gardens with nets and treats.
Month-end draw on the mana grid: the corridor lanterns burn noticeably dimmer tonight, and everyone complains about it like weather.
The Canteen kitchen is short-handed; the cook is offering an extra paid shift to whoever helps serve lunch.
The Cooking Club's ovens have run since dawn; the Canteen smells of honey bread and they are giving away the failures.
A formal duel challenge is chalked on the board outside the Sparring Pavilion. Nobody has signed to accept it yet.
Club recruiters have set up tables in the Courtyards, pressing leaflets on every first-year who slows down.
A Dragonchess match in the Mall's game halls has run into its second day; a crowd is betting points on it.
The Mall bakery has a new pastry out and the queue curls out of the door.
Sunday sorting at the Mail Tower is swamped; the sorting floor is asking anyone free to lend a hand.
A cart of heavy parcels has come in at the Mail Tower; locker tallies are going up all afternoon.
A rowing boat capsized near the willow island; the crew came back soaked and furious, and the boathouse is buzzing.
A clear, moonless dusk: the Observation Tower's instruments are already turning on their own, and the Divination Society has claimed the top deck.
An informal cross-dorm match has started on the Sports Field, and one side is a player short.
A misfired enchantment has left sparks hanging in the Workshop air for hours; the forges are shut until it settles.
Something in the Gardens grew far too well overnight; the Gardening Club is cutting a path back to the herb beds.
The Student Council is inspecting the dorm common rooms this evening: preservation lockers, quiet hours, the kettle rota.
The Announcement Pillars glow between periods: a lost-property amnesty at Reception, today only.
After today's Combat lessons the Medical Centre has a queue out of the door: sprains, burns and one badly singed eyebrow.
An airship passes low over the grounds on its way to the capital; half the Courtyards stops to watch.
Rumour in the common rooms: someone swears they counted four knocks at three o'clock last night.
Two late revisers are telling anyone who will listen that the main corridor ran long last night, after the night burn.
A cracked tree has come down at the Forest's edge; the Groundskeeper's Lodge wants volunteers with strong backs.
A Magic Theory study group has taken over a Study Room and is selling copies of its notes for points.
The warming runes on the Swimming Pool rim have failed; the water is ice-cold and the swim clubs are outraged.
A crown clerk from the Royal Inspectorate was seen carrying ledgers towards the Warden's Office. Nobody knows why.
Snow came down overnight and buried the paths; the Groundskeeper's Lodge is hiring a snow-clearing crew, 20 to 40 points a shift.
Yesterday's storm left branches and slipped roof slates across the grounds; the Groundskeeper's Lodge is paying a clean-up crew by the shift.
Dense fog lies over the grounds and the Doves have doubled their patrols, stopping anyone they cannot see clearly until it lifts.
